$comment2: textParam marks a component whose visible text is its own child text content rather than an attribute — app-button reads this.innerHTML (app-button.js:80), app-badge and app-tag are styled wrappers around their text. Without it the model can emit them and they render empty.
$comment: Hand-maintained decisions the generated design-system catalog cannot express: which components a generated surface may name, which take children or data as their first positional argument, and which attributes to withhold. gen-dsl-catalog.mjs merges this with design-system/catalog.json to produce dsl-catalog.json. Every component in catalog.json must have an entry here — `--check` fails otherwise, so a new component forces an explicit decision instead of silently becoming available or silently missing.

app-grid.note: columns takes an integer OR a grid-template string. app-grid.js:20 turns a positive integer into repeat(n, 1fr) and passes anything else through verbatim into style.setProperty('--grid-columns', …), which is the only way to express a ratio — app-row has no per-child sizing at all. The template form is a closed set rather than free text for two reasons: the value reaches a CSS custom property unfiltered and the DSL is written by a model, and a ratio carries meaning, so five named proportions are a vocabulary while arbitrary fr pairs are noise. Omitting columns entirely is the responsive option — the CSS default is repeat(auto-fill, minmax(300px, 1fr)) and setting columns replaces it, so both the integer and template forms are deliberate desktop shapes.

app-table.reason: The renderer registers the resolved rows as a synthetic source and sets data-fn itself. Leaving it settable would let a surface point the table at any registered source and bypass that.
app-table.note: Rows reach app-table as a fetcher on its `dataFn` property (app-table.js:24,113). Assigning the property avoids registering a synthetic source in the app-wide data-sources registry on every render pass — which never got unregistered and could collide with a real name.

app-accordion.note: Header text is the `label` attribute; the children are the body. Trailing header chips go through Slot("meta").

app-toolbar.note: Only useful with Slot() — its content is entirely start/end slotted.

app-stat-card.dslSummary: One metric standing on its own — label, value, and an optional delta with its trend arrow. For two or more headline metrics use AppStatRow, which separates them with hairlines and reserves the right skeleton.
app-stat-card.reason: The summary is the strongest place to say which of the two stat components to reach for, because it is read at the moment the model is choosing. Seventeen recorded AppStatCard calls across eleven fixtures and not one AppStatRow: the strip lost to a hand-built row of cards every time, and the design system calls it "the one stat strip". delta and trend stay — the DSL has real arithmetic (materialize.js:305), so a delta is @Last(rows.x) - @First(rows.x) and a trend is the sign of it. They were never once filled, but that is the prompt's failure to teach the computation, not a missing capability, and withholding them would remove a real one.

app-text.reason: The typography primitive. Nothing else in the vocabulary can put a heading above a group or a sentence beside a number, so without it every generated surface is a wall of boxes with no voice.

app-empty-state.reason: icon is withheld automatically now — it carries (markup) in its @attr line, so gen-catalog flags it and gen-dsl-catalog drops it. Listed here previously by hand, which is exactly the list that stops matching the code.

app-avatar.note: size/filled/interactive/disabled/state are CSS-only (app-avatar.css:86-113) rather than non-functional. They are absent from observedAttributes because nothing in JS re-runs on change; the renderer recreates elements per pass, so that costs nothing here.

app-button.reason: Route attributes are checked against the live router at render time, so href is admitted again; an unregistered path is dropped with a diagnostic naming it.

app-card.reason1b: Children land in `body`. app-card declares no `default` slot and rewrites innerHTML on render, so an unslotted child was appended and then wiped — `AppCard([chart], "Cost")`, the line the prompt itself teaches, built the chart and lost it with no diagnostic. `body` is the card's content region and the only slot a generic child can mean; leading/actions/footer are positions a surface would have to ask for by name.
app-card.reason: The card is the one container in the vocabulary, and until now nothing could go inside it. app-card declares four slots — leading, actions, body, footer — and every one of them was unreachable from DSL: children are only bound when childrenParam is set, so AppCard([chart], "Cost") put the chart into `name`, Slot("body", chart) had no children list to land in, and padding to a trailing position hit excess_arguments. Three recorded generations tried all three. Children lead here, as they do on app-modal, app-accordion and app-toolbar.
app-card.reason2: The attribute list is cut to what a generated dashboard can mean. What is left out is agent-catalog chrome the model can only reach by accident — and it did: chat-href sat at position 13 and a boolean landed in it, which is what non_route_value has been reporting. card-title is an alias for name kept for the replaced card's call sites; the model has no legacy call sites. Sixteen positions was itself the defect.

app-chart.note: Chart data is a JS property, not an attribute (app-chart.js:189). Two shapes by `type`: canvas forms (line/bar/donut) need Chart.js {labels, datasets}; row forms (hbar/progress) take a bare array of {label, value}. The renderer passes it through unchanged.

app-tabs.note: Panels are the children, each through Slot("<key>"); `tabs` names and orders them. The Action receives { key }. `strip` mode and `query-param` are page concerns and should not be set from a surface.

app-loading-bar.reason: Zero attributes; driven by global document events, not composition.

app-input.reason: Twenty-four positional slots is more than the generator can place. Every eval case that reached for app-input mis-slotted: $agentId written into "list" (slot 21), an Action at slot 27 past the end of the signature, another at "spellcheck" (slot 22), and 27 arguments passed for 24. Every control with twelve slots or fewer — app-search, app-segmented-control — reads four-for-four in the same corpus. The nine native input attributes below sit between `value` and `action`, and a generated dashboard has no use for any of them: `list` in particular names a <datalist> id a surface can never have produced. The other four sit in FRONT of `value`, which is the half that matters — withholding only the nine moves `action` to 15 and leaves `value` at 13, and "value is not read back from a $state" is one of the observed failures. So both groups go, and the signature lands at eleven: size, state, label, hint, required, disabled, type, placeholder, value, aria-label, action.
app-input.dslSummary: Free text the reader types or pastes — an agent id, a month as YYYY-MM, a name to look up. Its value has to be read back from the $state its own Action sets, or what is typed is discarded on the next repaint. Reach for AppSearch when the point is finding something in a list as you type, and AppSegmentedControl or AppSelect when the answer is one of a known few: a typed value the source matches exactly returns nothing for every near miss, with no error to say so.
app-input.note: A form control: its value plumbing is Action([@Set($var, …)]) on the trailing action slot, not an attribute.

app-select.note: A form control: its value plumbing is Action([@Set($var, …)]) on the trailing action slot, not an attribute.

app-segmented-control.note: A form control, same as app-select: its value plumbing is Action([@Set($var, …)]) on the trailing action slot. Segments come from the `items` attribute, so a generated surface can name them directly.

app-search.note: A form control: its value plumbing is Action([@Set($var, …)]) on the trailing action slot, not an attribute. nameFallback: the field has no visible label to fill in, so the component emits the placeholder as its accessible name when aria-label is absent — a floor, not the recommended path.

app-checkbox.note: A form control: its value plumbing is Action([@Set($var, …)]) on the trailing action slot, not an attribute.

app-radio.note: A form control: its value plumbing is Action([@Set($var, …)]) on the trailing action slot, not an attribute.

app-switch.note: A form control: its value plumbing is Action([@Set($var, …)]) on the trailing action slot, not an attribute.

app-chatbox.note: A form control: its value plumbing is Action([@Set($var, …)]) on the trailing action slot, not an attribute.

app-alert.dslSummary: Says that something is wrong or needs attention, in place: a source that failed, a quota nearly spent, a filter that matched nothing when it should have matched something. Use it when the surface has to tell the reader something the numbers alone do not. For a notice with an action attached, AppBanner.
app-alert.note: Inline status callout. Title/description are attributes; `variant` picks the feedback tone.

app-banner.dslSummary: One statement across the top of a surface, built around a single action — “Spend is 20% over budget. Review agents.” Use it when the whole surface needs saying something; when one panel is wrong, AppAlert.
app-banner.note: The child is the call to action (an app-button) and lands in the action slot; text is attributes.

app-spinner.reason: A bare indeterminate spinner. Every data component owns its own loading state and shows a skeleton shaped like the thing that is coming; a loose spinner is the model hand-rolling a state the runtime already has.

app-progress.dslSummary: A number against the ceiling it is measured against. Use it whenever how much is left matters as much as how much there is — a budget, a quota, seats in use. An AppStatCard states the figure; this states the proportion, which is the part a reader acts on. `value` is a PERCENT, 0–100, not the raw number: for 40 of 50 seats compute `40 / 50 * 100`. Passing 40 draws a bar at 40% for something that is 80% full, and nothing errors.

app-kbd.reason: Key caps for a keyboard shortcut. Nothing on a generated surface binds one.

app-breadcrumb.reason: A navigation trail. A generated surface is one route with nothing above it — the shell owns navigation, and a trail the surface invents would name places that do not exist.

app-trace-tree.dslSummary: A nested run where every node has a duration and an outcome: a trace's spans, a call graph, a build's steps. Use it when the nesting is the point — for a flat sequence of runs, AppTable or AppList says more per row.
app-trace-tree.note: Fully controlled: pass the whole tree in `spans`, the selected id in `value` and the folded ids in `collapsed`; it renders them and emits trace-tree-select / trace-tree-toggle rather than changing any of the three.

app-list.dslSummary: A few rows read downward rather than across. Use it instead of AppTable when there are no columns worth aligning — five agents with a status dot, the last handful of runs. A table earns its search, pager and sort headers at roughly ten rows and two columns worth sorting.
app-list.note: Children are app-list-item; selection is the caller's — bind list-select and set `selected` on the current item.

app-list-item.dslSummary: One AppList row: a heading, an optional description, a badge, a status dot. Only ever inside AppList.
app-list-item.note: Selection is bound on the parent app-list (list-select carries id + index); the item itself takes no Action. Its identifier is `value`.

app-field.dslSummary: Wraps a control in a label, a description and an error line. Use it when a control needs more than the one-line label it already carries — a filter whose effect is worth explaining, or one the reader can get wrong.
app-field.note: Wraps one control child with label/description/error. Not for app-input/app-select/app-search, which carry their own.

app-textarea.reason: Multi-line prose input. No data source takes prose, so anything typed here has nowhere to go.

app-slider.dslSummary: A threshold the reader drags. Use it for a filter over a continuous range — “only agents over $5”. For picking from a set, AppSegmentedControl or AppSelect.
app-slider.note: A form control: its value plumbing is Action([@Set($var, …)]) on the trailing action slot, not an attribute.

app-toggle.dslSummary: One thing on or off, shown as a pressed button. AppSwitch is the settings form of the same idea; reach for AppToggle inside an AppToggleGroup, or where the state reads as “this filter is applied” rather than “this setting is enabled”.

app-toggle-group.dslSummary: Several toggles acting as one control, single or multiple selection. Multiple is the reason it exists — AppSegmentedControl already covers the exclusive case, so use this one when more than one value can be on.
app-toggle-group.note: Children are app-toggle with a `value`; the group reflects the selection in its own `value`.

app-otp-input.reason: A one-time-passcode field. Authentication, never dashboard content.

app-tag-group.dslSummary: A row of tags acting as one filter, where several can be on at once — three of eight models. That is the case AppSegmentedControl cannot express, since it is one exclusive choice. Do not build this out of AppButtons.
app-tag-group.note: Children are app-tag; mode=none is a plain layout row.

app-pagination.reason: app-table brings its own pager. A second one has nothing to drive, and two pagers on one table is worse than none.

app-popover.reason: An anchored overlay with nothing of its own in it — a container for chrome. What it would hold belongs on the surface.

app-hover-card.reason: Reveals content on pointer rest. A dashboard should state what it knows; anything worth a hover card is worth a line.

app-menu.reason: An anchored popup of actions. Same class as app-context-menu: the actions a generated surface has are few enough to show.

app-context-menu.reason: A right-click menu. A hidden affordance the surface has no way to teach, on a page the reader did not build.

app-sheet.reason: A full-height side sheet over a backdrop. The Weave dock already owns the right-hand drawer; a surface opening a second one fights it.

app-calendar.reason: A full month grid for picking one date. app-date-field is the same choice in the space a dashboard has; the bare grid is a page's control, not a panel.

app-date-field.dslSummary: One specific day, picked from a calendar. Use it when a source takes a date rather than a window — fetchSpendCalendarDay's `date`. For a rolling window use AppSegmentedControl with 24h / 7d / 30d.
app-date-field.note: A form control: its value plumbing is Action([@Set($var, …)]) on the trailing action slot, not an attribute.

app-time-field.reason: An HH:MM editor. No data source in scope takes a time of day — the windows are days and ranges.

app-command.reason: A modal command palette is page chrome, not dashboard content; `groups` is a JSON tree of commands the surface cannot meaningfully author.

app-resizable.reason: Draggable panel dividers. Layout is declared with AppStack, AppRow and AppGrid — a surface that also ships a splitter is describing the same thing twice.

app-combobox.dslSummary: A picker that filters as you type. Use it instead of AppSelect when the list is long enough that scrolling is worse than typing — every agent, every model. For a five-item range filter, AppSelect or AppSegmentedControl.
app-combobox.note: Suggestions come from `data-fn` (a registered read source, `(query) => options`) or a static `options` list. The Action receives { value, option }.

$comment3: actionParam adds a trailing synthetic `action` parameter — the component has no such attribute; the renderer binds the Action to the element's trigger event. dslExcludeAttributes is the name weave2.0's dsl_prompt.py expects, so the two sides agree without translation.
$comment4: dataProp names the JS property a dataParam is assigned to; dataAsFetcher wraps the rows in an async () => ({data, total}) first. actionEvent overrides the event an Action is bound to — the default is the component's own 'change'/'input' event when it declares one, else 'click'.
